accountView.signInHint: Sign-in opens your web browser. The launcher never sees your password; it only receives a sign-in code from Microsoft.
accountView.notConfigured: Sign-in is unavailable in this build because no project-owned Microsoft application ID is configured (see docs/AUTH-SETUP.md).
accountView.waiting: Finish signing in with your web browser. This window updates automatically.
accountView.verified: Minecraft: Java Edition access verified for this session.
accountView.verifiedNote: Access is checked again every time you start the game.
accountView.signOutHint: Signing out removes the saved sign-in from this computer. It does not sign you out of Microsoft in your browser.
accountView.sessionOnly: The system credential store is unavailable, so you will need to sign in again after the launcher restarts.

stateTitle.app_not_approved: Launcher not approved by Minecraft services

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.microsoftHint: An account that has Minecraft: Java Edition plays the full game. You can add several and choose which one each installation uses.
accounts.notokenHint: Each profile is a player name for Minecraft's demo: five in-game days, no multiplayer. They make it easy to test installations without signing in.
accounts.notokenNone: No profiles yet. Without one, the demo plays as Player.
accounts.defaultNone: No default is chosen: installations play the demo as Player.
accounts.pendingSignOut: {name}: the saved sign-in could not be removed from this computer yet.
accounts.launcherHint: Your own account for friends and chats. You can also play as it: the game starts under its nick, as Minecraft's demo.
accounts.launcherWaiting: Finish in the window that opened.
accounts.launcherResent: A new letter is on its way.
accounts.launcherSignInAgain: The sign-in has ended. Sign in again.

launcherProblems.network: oauth.lapi.sh cannot be reached. Check the connection and try again.
launcherProblems.sign_in_again: The sign-in has ended. Sign in again.
launcherProblems.nick_reserved: This nick is reserved. Choose another.
launcherProblems.nick_invalid: A nick has 3 to 16 letters A–Z, digits or _.
launcherProblems.too_many: Too many attempts. Wait a little and try again.
launcherProblems.vault: The system credential store did not keep the sign-in; it lasts until the launcher closes.
launcherProblems.server: Something went wrong on the account server. Try again later.

instances.title: Installations
instances.empty: No installations yet. Create one to choose a Minecraft version.

install.otherBusy: Another operation is running. Install and repair are added to the queue and start after it.

explain.not_installed: The game files, the Java runtime and the version metadata are downloaded from Mojang and Adoptium and checked before use.
explain.ready: All files were verified. Repair checks every file again and replaces damaged ones.
explain.needs_verification: The files have not been fully verified since the last change. Verify them before playing.
explain.repair_required: Some files are damaged or missing. Repair replaces them.
explain.unsupported: This installation was created by a newer launcher version.

install.userData: Repair never changes worlds, screenshots or options in the game folder.
install.files: {done, number} of {total, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} verified

result.succeeded: {kind, select, repair {Repair} other {Installation}} finished. Downloaded {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} ({bytes}); reused {reused, plural, one {# verified file} other {# verified files}}.
result.cancelled: Cancelled. Files verified so far were kept; continue to resume.
result.interrupted: The launcher stopped before this finished. Files verified so far were kept.

install.offline: No internet connection. Installed versions still start; Microsoft accounts play without the online check, so multiplayer and Realms may not work. Installs and repairs wait in the queue until the connection returns.

createForm.title: New installation
createForm.name: Name

typeHints.snapshot: Test versions before a release. They can damage worlds; keep copies of worlds you care about.
typeHints.old_beta: Beta versions from 2010–2011. They run on Java 8 and have no demo mode, so playing needs a signed-in account.
typeHints.old_alpha: Alpha, Classic and pre-Classic versions from 2009–2010. They run on Java 8 and have no demo mode, so playing needs a signed-in account.

createForm.isolation: Each installation gets its own game folder for worlds, options and screenshots. The version cannot be changed later; create another installation to play a different version.
createForm.stale: Showing the last saved catalog because it could not be refreshed.
createForm.planRuntimeUnknown: Determined when the runtime is prepared
createForm.planNote: Based on the official metadata only. The version has not yet been checked by starting the game.

hints.fabric: A lightweight loader for Fabric mods.
hints.quilt: A loader for Quilt mods that also runs most Fabric mods.
hints.forge: The long-standing loader for Forge mods. Installing runs the Forge installer, which builds the modded game with the installation's Java.
hints.neoforge: The successor of Forge for NeoForge mods. Installing runs its installer, which builds the modded game with the installation's Java.

loaders.gamesHint: Only Minecraft versions that {loader} supports are listed.
loaders.modsHint: Put mods into the mods folder inside the installation's game folder. You can change the loader version later in Settings → Installations.
loaders.sources: The {loader} files come from its project's own servers and are checked the same way.

details.title: Installation settings
details.openFolderHint: Worlds, screenshots and options of this installation are stored there.
details.memoryHint: Between {min, number, ::group-off} and {max, number, ::group-off} MiB on this computer.
details.lowMemory: This computer has less than 8 GiB of memory. The game may run poorly with the available amount.
details.resolutionHint: Width {minWidth, number, ::group-off}–{maxWidth, number, ::group-off}, height {minHeight, number, ::group-off}–{maxHeight, number, ::group-off} pixels.
details.busy: This installation is busy; its settings cannot change right now.
details.notesHint: Only for you: what this installation is for, its mods, servers or anything to remember.
details.gameArgumentsHint: Added after the game's own arguments, for example --quickPlaySingleplayer "My World" to open a world at start. Quotes keep spaces inside one value. The player, folders, window size and fullscreen are set by the launcher.

memory.limited: Recommended: {mib, number, ::group-off} MiB for {reason}; it would use about {wanted, number, ::group-off} MiB, but this computer has room for less.
memory.perKind: Recommended for each kind of installation
memory.perKindHint: Minecraft 1.12.2 and older: 2048 MiB; newer Minecraft: 3072 MiB; with a mod loader: 4096 MiB, more once it holds many mods. Never more than half of this computer's memory.
memory.fixed: The same for every new installation
memory.fixedLine: Memory: {mib, number, ::group-off} MiB (your setting for new installations).

workload.modded: a mod loader with {mods, plural, =0 {no mods yet} one {# mod} other {# mods}}

crash.title: Why the game stopped
crash.summary: The game stopped: {title}. The cause and what to do are shown with the installation.
crash.suspects: Mods the crash report points at: {mods}

jvm_option.title: Java did not accept a JVM option
jvm_option.cause: This Java does not understand the JVM option {option}, so the game could not start.
jvm_option.fix: Remove or correct it in the installation's JVM options, or choose a Java that knows it.

heap_unavailable.title: Java could not reserve the memory
heap_unavailable.cause: Java could not set aside {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB for the game. The computer has less free memory than that, or the Java is 32-bit.
heap_unavailable.fix: Lower the installation's memory or close other programs. The launcher's own Java is 64-bit.

java_too_old.title: The game needs a newer Java
java_too_old.cause: {required, select, none {The game or one of its mods needs a newer Java} other {The game or one of its mods needs Java {required}}}{found, select, none {.} other {, but Java {found} started it.}}
java_too_old.fix: Choose the launcher's Java for this installation; it picks the version the game needs. If you chose your own Java, choose a newer one.

java_too_new.title: The game needs an older Java
java_too_new.cause: This Minecraft or mod loader was made for an older Java{found, select, none {} other { and does not run on Java {found}}}. Minecraft 1.16 and older with mod loaders usually needs Java 8.
java_too_new.fix: Choose the launcher's Java for this installation, or your own Java 8.

missing_dependency.title: A mod needs another mod
missing_dependency.cause: {mod} needs {dependency}{required, select, none {} other { ({required})}}, which is not installed.{count, plural, =1 {} other { # requirements are missing in all.}}
missing_dependency.fix: Add {dependency} for this Minecraft version and mod loader to the mods folder, or remove {mod}.

wrong_dependency_version.title: A mod needs another version of a mod
wrong_dependency_version.cause: {mod} needs {dependency}{required, select, none {} other { {required}}}{found, select, none {} other {, but {found} is installed}}.{count, plural, =1 {} other { # requirements are unmet in all.}}
wrong_dependency_version.fix: Update {dependency} in the mods folder to the version {mod} asks for, or use an older {mod}.

wrong_minecraft_version.title: A mod is made for another Minecraft version
wrong_minecraft_version.cause: {mod} needs Minecraft {required}{found, select, none {} other {, but this installation is {found}}}.
wrong_minecraft_version.fix: Download the {mod} file made for this Minecraft version, or remove it.

loader_too_old.title: A mod needs a newer mod loader
loader_too_old.cause: {mod, select, none {A mod} other {{mod}}} needs a newer {dependency, select, none {mod loader} other {{dependency}}}{required, select, none {} other { ({required})}}{found, select, none {} other {; this installation has {found}}}.
loader_too_old.fix: Choose a newer loader version in the installation's settings, or use an older version of the mod.

incompatible_mods.title: Two mods cannot run together
incompatible_mods.fix: Remove one of them from the mods folder.

duplicate_mods.title: A mod is installed twice
duplicate_mods.cause: {modId, select, none {The same mod is installed more than once.} other {The mod {modId} is installed more than once{files, select, none {.} other {: {files}.}}}}
duplicate_mods.fix: Keep only one file of it, the newest, in the mods folder.

mod_for_other_loader.title: A mod is made for another loader
mod_for_other_loader.cause: {file, select, none {Some files in the mods folder are {loader, select, none {made for another loader} other {{loader} mods}}, so this installation's loader skips them.} other {{file} is {loader, select, none {made for another loader} other {a {loader} mod}}, so this installation's loader skips it.}}
mod_for_other_loader.fix: Remove it, or download the version made for this installation's loader.

corrupt_mod_file.title: A file is damaged
corrupt_mod_file.cause: {file, select, none {A game or mod file} other {{file}}} is damaged or incomplete, often after an interrupted download.
corrupt_mod_file.fix: {place, select, mods {Delete it from the mods folder and download it again.} other {Repair the installation to download it again.}}

corrupt_config.title: A config file is damaged
corrupt_config.cause: {file, select, none {A config file} other {The config file {file}}} could not be read: it is damaged or empty, often after the computer shut down while the game was running.
corrupt_config.fix: Delete it from the config folder; the game creates it again with default settings.

mixin_failed.title: A mod could not change the game's code
mixin_failed.cause: {modId, select, none {A mod} other {The mod {modId}}} failed to apply its changes to the game (Mixin). It is usually made for another version of Minecraft or of another mod, or conflicts with another mod.
mixin_failed.fix: Update or remove this mod; its page lists the version for this Minecraft and loader.

mod_failed_to_load.title: A mod failed to start
mod_failed_to_load.cause: {modId, select, none {A mod} other {The mod {modId}}} hit an error while the loader started it.
mod_failed_to_load.fix: Update or remove it. If the crash is new, remove the mods you added last.

optifine_conflict.title: OptiFine does not work here
optifine_conflict.cause: OptiFine does not work with this loader version or with other mods, such as Sodium, Embeddium or Rubidium.
optifine_conflict.fix: Remove OptiFine, or use the OptiFine release made for exactly this Forge version. With Fabric, use Sodium and Iris instead.

out_of_memory.title: The game ran out of memory
out_of_memory.cause: The game used all {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB it was given.
out_of_memory.fix: Give the installation more memory: {suggested, number, ::group-off} MiB is a good start. Many mods, shaders or a long render distance need more.

pack_needs_memory.title: The modpack asks for more memory
pack_needs_memory.cause: {required, select, none {The modpack needs more memory than this installation gives the game.} other {The modpack needs at least {required} MiB, but this installation gives the game {memory} MiB.}}
pack_needs_memory.fix: {required, select, none {Give the installation more memory in its settings, then start again.} other {Give the installation at least {required} MiB in its settings, then start again.}}

system_memory.title: The computer ran out of memory
system_memory.cause: Java could not get memory from the system. Other programs use the rest, or the {memory, number, ::group-off} MiB given to the game leave too little for everything else.
system_memory.fix: Close other programs or lower the installation's memory. On Windows a larger paging file also helps.

killed.title: The game was killed
killed.cause: The system or another program ended the game at once. On Linux this is usually the out-of-memory killer, when the computer runs out of memory.
killed.fix: Close other programs or lower the installation's memory, then start again.

opengl_unsupported.title: The graphics driver offers no suitable OpenGL
opengl_unsupported.cause: The game could not open its window because the graphics driver does not offer the OpenGL version Minecraft needs{error, select, none {} other { (GLFW error {error})}}.
opengl_unsupported.fix: Install the newest driver from the graphics card's maker (AMD, Intel or NVIDIA), not the one Windows chose. On a laptop, run Java on the dedicated graphics card.

graphics_driver.title: The graphics driver crashed
graphics_driver.cause: The game crashed inside the {vendor, select, amd {AMD} intel {Intel} nvidia {NVIDIA} mesa {Mesa} other {graphics}} driver ({module}).
graphics_driver.fix: Update or reinstall the graphics driver from the maker's site. Shaders and overlays can set it off too: try without them.

overlay.title: An overlay crashed the game
overlay.cause: {program, select, none {A program that draws over games} other {{program}, a program that draws over games,}} crashed the game.
overlay.fix: Turn off overlays and recorders (RivaTuner or MSI Afterburner, the Discord overlay, OBS game capture, D3DGear, the NVIDIA overlay) and start again.

native_crash.title: The game crashed outside Java
native_crash.cause: The game crashed in native code{module, select, none {} other { ({module})}}{signal, select, none {} other {, {signal}}}. Graphics drivers, overlays, antivirus software or a damaged Java are the usual causes.
native_crash.fix: Update the graphics driver, turn off overlays and repair the installation. The JVM error file (hs_err) in the game folder has the details.

missing_native_library.title: A game library is missing
missing_native_library.cause: The game could not load its native library{library, select, none {} other { {library}}}.
missing_native_library.fix: Repair the installation to download it again. Antivirus software sometimes removes these files.

broken_installation.title: Game files are incomplete
broken_installation.cause: Files the game or Java needs are missing or damaged.

disk_full.title: The disk is full
disk_full.cause: The game could not write a file because the disk has no free space.
disk_full.fix: Free space on the disk that holds the launcher's data, then start again.

file_access.title: A file could not be used
file_access.cause: {file, select, none {A file} other {The file {file}}} is locked by another program or may not be read or written.
file_access.fix: Close programs that may use it (another copy of the game, a backup or sync program, antivirus software) and start again.

world_load_failed.title: The world could not be loaded
world_load_failed.cause: The game failed while reading a world ({description}).
world_load_failed.fix: Restore the world from a backup. If a mod was removed or updated, put back the version the world was made with.

ticking_entity.title: An entity crashes the world
ticking_entity.cause: {entity, select, none {An entity} other {The entity {entity}}}{position, select, none {} other { at {position}}} crashes the game every time it updates.
ticking_entity.fix: Restore the world from a backup, or update or remove the mod that adds this entity.

ticking_block_entity.title: A block crashes the world
ticking_block_entity.cause: {block, select, none {A block} other {The block {block}}}{position, select, none {} other { at {position}}} crashes the game every time it updates.
ticking_block_entity.fix: Restore the world from a backup, or update or remove the mod that adds this block.

server_hang.title: The game froze
server_hang.cause: The game stopped responding{seconds, select, none {} other { for {seconds} seconds}} and its watchdog ended it. Large builds, many mods or too little memory cause this.
server_hang.fix: Give the game more memory and update or remove the mods named in the crash report. If one world causes it, restore it from a backup.

debug_crash.title: Crash by F3 + C
debug_crash.cause: The crash was started on purpose by holding F3 + C.
debug_crash.fix: Nothing is broken. Holding F3 + C for ten seconds crashes the game to test it.

game_crash.title: The game crashed
game_crash.cause: The game wrote a crash report: “{description}”{exception, select, none {.} other {: {exception}}}
game_crash.fix: Open the crash report for details. If mods are named here, update or remove them first.

terminated.title: Another program ended the game
terminated.cause: Another program asked the game to stop; it was not the launcher's Stop button.
terminated.fix: If it was not you, look for a program that ends other programs, then start again.

console_question.title: The game waited for an answer it could not get
console_question.cause: The game asked a question in a console window, which the launcher cannot show, and kept asking. The launcher ended it.
console_question.fix: Read the lines below: they usually name the problem, such as a damaged file or too little memory. Fix it and start again.

unknown.title: The game exited with an error
unknown.cause: {exitCode, select, none {The game stopped} other {The game exited with code {exitCode}}} and printed no cause the launcher knows.
unknown.fix: Look at the output below and the crash reports. If it started after a change, undo it: remove the mods or options you added last.

reports.offer: Send a report to the developers
reports.title: Report to the developers
reports.intro: The report helps fix crashes and explain them better. You see everything below before anything is sent.
reports.privacy: Chat, player names, IP and server addresses, world names, IDs and your home folder are removed. Mod names and versions stay.
reports.removed: Removed: {chatLines, number} chat lines, {names, number} names, {addresses, number} addresses, {worlds, number} world names, {ids, number} IDs.
reports.noteHint: For example: the game crashed when I opened a world after adding mods.
reports.sent: Thank you! The report was sent.
reports.queued: The service cannot be reached now. The report is kept and sent by itself later.

failureKinds.panic: An internal error stopped part of the launcher.
failureKinds.frontend: An error happened in the launcher window.
failureKinds.unclean_exit: The launcher did not close properly last time.

reports.failureBody: You can send a report so the developers can fix it. You will see everything before it is sent.

deleteInstance.holds: Its game folder holds {size}, including what you made or added:
deleteInstance.resourcePacks: {count, plural, one {# resource pack} other {# resource packs}}
deleteInstance.shaderPacks: {count, plural, one {# shader pack} other {# shader packs}}
deleteInstance.offerBackup: Back it up first? A backup of the whole installation can bring it back later from Backups.
deleteInstance.nothing: It holds no worlds, mods, packs or screenshots.
deleteInstance.shared: Game files shared with other installations (libraries, assets, Java) stay.
deleteInstance.busy: Wait until the running operation or game ends.
deleteInstance.deletedWithBackup: "{name}" was backed up and deleted. Backups can bring it back.

settings.title: Settings

sectionHints.general: Language, appearance, the launcher window while you play, and where data is kept.
sectionHints.java: Which Java runtimes the launcher downloads for new installations.
sectionHints.defaults: Memory, window size and fullscreen given to each new installation.
sectionHints.network: Metered connections, the traffic the launcher downloads, and where downloads come from.
sectionHints.installations: Memory, window, fullscreen, Minecraft arguments, mod loader version and Java of an existing installation.
sectionHints.privacy: What the launcher sends to its developers, and only with your consent.
sectionHints.reset: Put chosen parts of the launcher back to how they were at first start.

javaProviderHints.mojang: The runtimes the official Minecraft launcher uses, with the exact Java each version asks for. Where Mojang publishes none for this computer, Temurin is used.
javaProviderHints.temurin: Current Eclipse Temurin builds of the Java version each Minecraft version needs.

settings.javaApplies: Applies to new installations. To change the Java of an installed version, or to use your own, open Installations.

instanceJava.title: Java of this installation
instanceJava.managedHint: Downloaded and checked by the launcher. A different source is downloaded at the next repair.
instanceJava.customHint: A Java installed on this computer. The launcher checks its version against the game and warns about a mismatch.
instanceJava.installFirst: Install this version first to choose your own Java.
instanceJava.jvmHint: Added after the version's own options; for the same option the later one wins. Each option starts with "-" and takes its value after "=", for example -XX:+UseG1GC -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8.
instanceJava.checked: Java {version} ({vendor}, {arch}). This game was built for Java {required}.

issues.older: This Java is older than the Java {required} this game needs. The game will most likely not start.
issues.newer: This Java is newer than the Java {required} this game was built for. Recent versions usually run; older versions and mod loaders often fail.
issues.architecture: This Java is built for another processor ({arch}). The game may not start or may run slowly.

instanceJava.accepted: You chose this Java despite a warning:
instanceJava.pendingSwitch: Java from {provider} is downloaded at the next repair.

instanceLoader.title: Mod loader version
instanceLoader.hint: Newest first. Installing the other version keeps the game files, mods and worlds.
instanceLoader.warning: Mods made for {loader} {from} may not work with {to}. Back up your worlds first if they matter. The new loader is installed right away.

duringGameModes.unload_and_return: Close the launcher window and reopen it when the game exits
duringGameModes.close_launcher: Close the launcher once the game window opens; the game keeps running

settings.readOnly: Settings are read-only because they were written by a newer launcher version or could not be read.

modes.default: The per-user folder the operating system provides.
modes.portable: Portable mode: the data is next to the launcher, so the whole folder can move to another computer.

dataFolder.toDefault: Move back to the default folder
dataFolder.confirmHint: If that folder already holds launcher data from before, the launcher switches to it without copying. Otherwise installations, Java, game files and settings are copied; the current folder is kept, so you can delete it afterwards. The launcher uses the new folder from its next start. Copying can take a while.
dataFolder.copying: Copying the data… The console window shows progress.
dataFolder.pending: The data was copied. Quit and start the launcher again to use
dataFolder.busy: Wait until the running operation or game ends to move the data.
dataFolder.portableHint: Portable mode keeps the data in a launcher-data folder next to the launcher; delete the portable.txt file there to stop. Sign-ins stay with this computer's credential store.
dataFolder.pendingReused: The launcher will use the data already in that folder. Quit and start the launcher again to use

hints.installations: Deletes {count, plural, one {the # installation} other {all # installations}} with their game folders: worlds, mods, settings and screenshots.
hints.gameFiles: {size}: libraries, assets, Java and version files shared by installations. Installed versions download them again at their next repair.
hints.backups: Deletes {count, plural, one {# backup} other {# backups}} ({size}).
hints.accounts: Signs out {microsoft, plural, one {# Microsoft account} other {# Microsoft accounts}} and removes {profiles, plural, one {# profile} other {# profiles}} without an account.
hints.settings: Theme, defaults for new installations, Java source, metered connection and automatic backups. The language and the data folder stay.
hints.traffic: Forgets the traffic counted this month and before.
hints.temporary: {size}: unfinished downloads, thumbnails and game logs.

reset.userData: These installations hold what you made or added:
reset.backUpFirst: Back them up before deleting (each as a whole installation; Backups can bring it back)
reset.backupsKept: Existing backups are deleted first; the new ones are kept.
reset.busy: Reset waits until the running operation or game ends.
reset.done: Reset done: {installations, plural, one {# installation} other {# installations}} deleted ({backedUp} backed up first), {backups, plural, one {# backup} other {# backups}} deleted, {accounts, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} signed out; {size} freed.

privacy.shareStatsHint: After a crash, its kind, the launcher, game and loader versions and the system are counted. No logs, names or install ID are sent.
privacy.reports: Crash reports are sent only when you press Send after reading them. They carry a random install ID so reports from one computer can be read together.
privacy.installIdNone: Not created yet: it appears with your first report.
privacy.newInstallIdHint: With a new ID, later reports are not linked to earlier ones.

runs.drainTimedOut: Output capture was closed 2 seconds after exit because another process kept the output open.
runs.dropped: {count, plural, one {# earlier line} other {# earlier lines}} not shown.
runs.stopWarning: Stopping ends Minecraft immediately. Anything not saved in the current world is lost. Quit from the game menu to save.
runs.loggingDegraded: The output log could not be written to disk; the last lines are still shown here.

harness.title: Lifecycle test (debug build only)
harness.explanation: Starts a harmless copy of this launcher as a child process to test closing and reopening the window. It cannot run any other program and is not part of release builds.

quit.dialogBody: Quitting now would stop it. Stopping a game may lose unsaved progress. You can keep the launcher running in the background instead; open it again to return.
quit.jobTitle: Game files are still being prepared
quit.jobBody: Quitting now cancels the installation or repair; files verified so far are kept for next time. Keep it running in the background and the launcher window returns when it finishes.

console.title: Console
console.openHint: Everything the launcher does and everything the game prints, live, in a separate window (Ctrl+Shift+L).
console.empty: Nothing yet. Install or start a game to see its output here.
console.count: {shown, number} of {total, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
console.missed: {count, plural, one {# older line was} other {# older lines were}} dropped (the console keeps the newest 10,000).
console.unreachable: The launcher core does not answer. Lines will appear again when it does.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.exportExplanation: Creates a ZIP file you can attach to a support request. It contains launcher and system information, installation versions and health, recent operation results and the launcher-captured output of the last three runs. Home and launcher folder paths are shortened and sign-in tokens are removed.
diagnostics.exportExcluded: Never included: account records, sign-in tokens, launch argument files, worlds, screenshots, options or other files from game folders.

about.title: About
about.license: License: not chosen yet. The project owner has not published a license for this source code.

foundation.title: Project status
foundation.body: Installing, repairing and launching are implemented. Starting the game needs Microsoft sign-in, which this build cannot offer until the project supplies its own Microsoft application ID.

systemInfo.title: Launcher core
systemInfo.errorPrefix: The launcher core could not be reached:

errorCodes.AUTH_TIMEOUT: Sign-in was not completed in time. Start sign-in again.
errorCodes.AUTH_STATE_MISMATCH: The sign-in response does not belong to this sign-in. Start sign-in again.
errorCodes.AUTH_APP_NOT_APPROVED: Minecraft services have not approved this launcher yet.
errorCodes.AUTH_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED: This account is restricted, for example by Microsoft family settings.
errorCodes.AUTH_FORBIDDEN: The sign-in service refused this request.

backups.title: Backups
backups.hint: A backup stores each file once: a new backup only adds what changed since earlier ones. Back up single worlds or the whole installation. Game files that Repair can download again are not included.
backups.afterPlay: Back up changed worlds after playing
backups.afterPlayHint: When a game session ends, every world it changed is backed up automatically.
backups.keepHint: Older automatic backups are deleted. Backups you make yourself stay until you delete them.
backups.noWorlds: This installation has no worlds yet.
backups.wholeHint: Worlds, mods, settings, resource packs and shader packs of this installation.
backups.confirmRestore: Replace {what} with the backup from {date}? Its current state is backed up first.
backups.confirmDelete: Delete the backup from {date}? Files other backups use are kept.
backups.busy: Backups and restores wait until the running operation or game ends.
backups.deletedHint: Backups of installations that were deleted. A backup of a whole installation brings it back with its worlds, mods and settings; then install it to play.
backups.broughtBack: "{name}" is back. Install it to play.

gallery.title: Screenshots
gallery.hint: Screenshots from every installation, grouped by installation and game version. Press F2 in the game to take one.

metered.toggleHint: Ask before big downloads and watch the traffic. Turn it on for mobile data or a plan with a data cap.
metered.warn: Ask before downloads of at least, MiB
metered.limitHint: A download that would pass it always asks first. 0 means no limit.

metered.confirmReset: Forget all traffic counted so far?
metered.approvalLarge: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} ({size}) will be downloaded over a metered connection.

network.offlineHint: No internet connection. Installed versions still start; installs and repairs wait in the queue until it returns.

mirror.title: Download source

hints.automatic: Original sites first; the launcher's mirror when one fails, is very slow or lost a file.
hints.mirror_first: For connections where original sites are blocked or very slow. They stay the fallback.
hints.origin_only: Never use the mirror. Downloads wait when a site is down.

mirror.checked: Every file is checked against its checksum, whichever site it comes from.
mirror.inUse: Not reachable now: {sites}. Downloading from the launcher's mirror.

updates.title: Launcher {version}
updates.availableBody: Download it now; it installs when you close the launcher.

updates.readyShort: Downloaded; installs when you close the launcher.

settings.title: Updates

modes.auto: Download and install when I close the launcher

settings.notConfigured: This build does not look for updates.

channel.title: Versions
channel.betaHint: Beta versions come before stable ones and may have problems. If a new version does not start, the launcher goes back to the one before.
channel.stableHint: Going back to stable: you keep this version until a newer stable one comes out.
